messages:
Sarah: Heads-up — I'm bringing Pacifica-v1 into staging for wider multilingual smoke tests. Quick summary: zh->en BLEU drop vs baseline, Korean polite/honorific suffixes sometimes missing, and Arabic bracket mirroring + RTL punctuation flips in some samples. Anyone seen something like this after a model/quant bring-up?
Li: Repro steps? sample inputs? I can run quick checks.
Sarah: repro samples below (short). Noting this happens more on int8 quantized builds.
Sarah: ```
# curl test (staging endpoint)
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/pacifica/v1/generate -d '{"input":"简体中文：明天 2026年5月1日 去机场 怎么走？","lang":"zh"}'
```
Li: ran that, baseline (aegis-lite) returns fluent chunk; Pacifica sometimes inserts extra spaces and splits the numeric tokens: "2026年 5月1日" -> "2026 年 5 月 1 日" which breaks downstream detok heuristics.
Hiro: I ran a batch of 200 zh-en pairs — automated BLEU: baseline 31.2 -> Pacifica 27.6 (staging int8). Also saw Korea example: input "선생님께서 감사합니다" -> Pacifica -> "선생님께 감사" (dropped polite suffix).
Miguel: curious if tokenizer merge table changed or there was a new normalization step. Any recent tokenizer commits or vocabulary shuffles? @Jun?
Jun: I pushed a tiny tokenizer cleanup last week (normalize-nfkc) but that was only for the training pipeline. No vocab shuffles. However we did flip an int8 kernel path in runtime-rtx that might change subtokenization alignment for cached prefix BPE.
Li: here's quick tokenizer dump for the zh sample (Pacifica token ids):
```
# pseudo-output
Tokens: [3456, 120, 78, 90, 2026, 11, 5, 1]
Detok: "简体 中文： 明天 2026 年 5 月 1 日 去 机场 怎么 走 ？"
```
Hiro: Also saw Arabic bracket/mirror issue on bidi runs: "(مرحبا)" becomes ")مرحبا(" in output occasionally. That looks like bidi rendering switch rather than tokenization. Might be a directionality marker lost in detok.
Miguel: Possible action items: 1) bisect runtime kernel flip (Jun) 2) run tokenizer-only inference (no quant) to isolate 3) add a small eval set for honorifics + numerals + RTL brackets.
Jun: I'll start a bisect on the runtime change range (commit range: rtx@c3f..c3f+10). ETA ~1h.
eval-bot: smoke-eval results uploaded: https://internal.redwood/evals/pacifica/staging/6145678901 — zh-en BLEU: 27.6, baseline 31.2; ko-honorific precision drop 0.08; ar-bidi-bracket-flips: 12/200 samples. :warning:
Sarah: thanks — assigning: Jun (runtime bisect), Li (tokenizer dumps + detok logs), Hiro (evaluate polite-suffix harness + add failing cases), Miguel (rollout guard + canary config). Can we hold canary to 10% until we have a root cause?
Li: noted, I'll attach tokenization diffs to the ticket.
Jun: bisect found a suspect change: selector for fused-kernel fallback altered loop ordering; test-run without that change reproduces baseline-like token alignment. Patching a quick fix to test.
Hiro: after Jun's patch, reran 50-sample smoke: BLEU improved to 30.9, ko suffix issues reduced to 2/50, ar bracket flips 0/50. Looks promising.
Sarah: great. let's keep the canary at 5% and roll patch into staging. Add regression unit tests for numerals, honorifics, and bidi brackets. :thumbsup:
Miguel: filed rollout stop-gap: disable the new fused-kernel path for int8 until patched.
Sarah: closing loop — please post final PR/commit IDs in this thread when merged.
Jun: PR  #8421 opened (runtime: fix fused-kernel loop order).
Li: attached tokenizer dump + failing example list in the ticket.
eval-bot: final-smoke summary will be appended to the ticket after nightly run.
